categories.main_business_segments: AZOOM operates two main business segments: the Idle Asset Utilization Business and the Visualization Business. The Idle Asset Utilization Business focuses on IT-driven solutions for underutilized real estate, primarily specializing in monthly parking lot introduction and subleasing services. The Visualization Business, led by subsidiary CGworks, provides 3DCG and VR-based visualization services for real estate and architectural clients.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary IT platforms, such as the CarParking portal for monthly parking lot search and management, and develops web-based reservation and management systems for rental spaces. In the Visualization segment, advanced 3DCG and VR technologies are used to create high-quality graphics and virtual tours, with recent adoption of generative AI for rendering services. System development is supported by offshore teams in Vietnam.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers for the Idle Asset Utilization Business include parking lot owners, real estate owners, and end-users seeking monthly parking spaces, as well as operators of rental spaces like meeting rooms and gyms. The Visualization Business serves display, architecture, interior design, and real estate industries, particularly companies involved in large-scale developments, commercial facilities, and property renovations.
categories.geographic_coverage: AZOOM's primary operations are in Japan, with service coverage across all prefectures for parking lot introduction and major metropolitan areas for subleasing. The company also has development and production subsidiaries in Vietnam (Hanoi and Da Nang), supporting both business segments. Over 90% of revenue is generated from domestic Japanese customers.
categories.supply_chain_position: AZOOM operates at the midstream and downstream points of the supply chain. In the parking business, it acts as an intermediary and service provider between property owners and end-users, while also taking on subleasing (master lease) roles. In visualization, it is a B2B service provider delivering digital content to client companies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the monthly parking lot platform's reach and database, enhancing IT-driven operational efficiency, and diversifying into new web-based reservation and management services for idle spaces. The company is also focused on strengthening its 3DCG/VR capabilities, expanding AI-driven rendering services, and leveraging offshore development to maximize profitability. ESG and sustainability, including climate adaptation and diversity, are also emphasized.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through a mix of transaction-based fees (introduction and contract fees from parking lot owners and users), recurring rental income from subleasing (master lease) arrangements, SaaS subscription fees for reservation systems, and project-based sales of visualization content. The company also earns guarantee fees through its subsidiary for rent guarantee services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In the monthly parking lot segment, AZOOM competes with other online parking search platforms and traditional real estate agencies, with differentiation based on IT integration and nationwide coverage. In subleasing, competition includes other property management and leasing firms. The visualization segment faces competition from other 3DCG and VR content providers, but AZOOM positions itself as a technology-driven, quality-focused player with offshore cost advantages.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending September 2025, consolidated sales reached 13.48 billion yen, up 27.9% year-on-year, with operating profit of 2.61 billion yen (up 43%). Net income attributable to shareholders was 1.83 billion yen (up 42.2%). The company has demonstrated strong, consistent growth in both revenue and profit over the past five years, with a workforce of 455 employees and a high equity ratio (76.7%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: AZOOM's unique value lies in its integration of IT and real estate expertise, offering the largest database of monthly parking lots in Japan and seamless online-to-offline solutions for both owners and users. Its subleasing model provides stable income and operational outsourcing for property owners. In visualization, the company differentiates through high-quality 3DCG/VR content, rapid delivery, and cost efficiency via offshore production, as well as innovative AI-based rendering services.
